'المجلس'`. Use it in journal/page.tsx (the metadata through generateMetadata, and the RoomHero title), in journal/[slug]/page.tsx lines 55 and 88, and pass it to HomeView and BookView in place of the literals in src/content/home.ts:32 and BookView.tsx:212.
verifierCorrections: The approach is right, with two additions. findings.title: Book page hero cover (the page's LCP image) states the wrong `sizes`, so phones and tablets download the 1200w file (399 KB) when the 720w file (133 KB) is enough; it also has no fetchPriority
findings.evidence:
<Picture id={BOOK.cover.id} alt={BOOK.cover.alt} sizes="(min-width: 1024px) 400px, 70vw" loading="eager" />

book.module.css:9-11
.cover {
  flex: 0 1 min(400px, 40%);
  min-inline-size: 220px;
findings.failureScenario: The cover is laid out at max(220px, min(400px, 40% of the band's content width)), and `flex-grow: 0` keeps that width after the hero wraps. The `sizes` value says 70vw below 1024px. Worked examples: a 390px iPhone at DPR 3 renders the cover at 220px (56vw), but sizes gives 273px, i.e. 819 device px, so the browser picks khous-cover-b-1200.webp (398,806 B) instead of the 720w file (133,270 B). A 768px tablet at DPR 2 renders it at 276px (36vw), but sizes gives 538px, i.e. 1076 device px, so it again picks the 1200w file. That is roughly 265 KB extra on the image that is the largest element of /book's first screen on mobile. Unlike the home portrait and the journal empty state, the cover is also eager with no `fetchPriority="high"`, so it competes at default priority with the two preloaded fonts and the CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: In src/components/public/book/BookView.tsx line 44, make `sizes` match the layout and prioritise the image: `sizes="(min-width: 1024px) 400px, (min-width: 560px) 40vw, 220px" loading="eager" fetchPriority="high"`.

findings.title: With JavaScript off, or before hydration, the contact form sends the visitor's name, email and message in the URL, then silently loses the message
findings.evidence:
<form id="contact-form" className={styles.form} noValidate onSubmit={submit} aria-label="راسلني">
...
<input ref={nameRef} id="contact-name" name="name" ...
...
<ActionButton type="submit" arrow disabled={!turnstileAvailable || status.kind === 'sending'}>
  أرسل
</ActionButton>
findings.failureScenario: The production build has NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY set, so the static HTML renders «أرسل» enabled (useTurnstile returns available: Boolean(siteKey)). The form has no method or action, and its fields carry name="name"/"email"/"message"/"website". A visitor with JavaScript off fills in the form and presses «أرسل» or Enter. The browser submits natively: GET /contact?name=…&email=…&message=…&website=. Cloudflare serves contact.html, the page reloads empty, nothing is shown, and nothing reaches the contact function. The personal data and the whole message stay in the address bar and browser history, and go out in the same-origin Referer on every subresource request. The same thing happens with JavaScript on if the visitor submits before React hydrates (slow phone network). There is no <noscript> notice. The D39 evidence screenshot contact-768-nojs.png shows the enabled «أرسل», with an empty Turnstile gap above it. The JS-off e2e covers only '/', the rooms and '/book'.
findings.suggestedFix: In ContactForm.tsx, gate submission on hydration the way BookPreview.tsx already does: `const scripted = useSyncExternalStore(noSubscribe, () => true, () => false)`, then `disabled={!scripted || !turnstileAvailable || status.kind === 'sending'}`. A disabled default button also blocks implicit Enter submission. Add a <noscript> line inside the form: «الإرسال يحتاج JavaScript؛ راسلني عبر القنوات المجاورة.»

findings.title: بدأتُ من هنا: the «تظهر المقاطع هنا» films can silently disappear, depending on the movement's first text block
findings.evidence:
const withFigure = b === 0 && movement.vignette
let before: Para[] = block.paras
let after: Para[] = []
if (b === 0 && movement.films) [before, after] = splitAfterFirstDisplay(block.paras)
...
{after.length > 0 && (
  <>
    <Films reels={room.media.reels} />
findings.failureScenario: Films render only when block 0 of the marked movement is text, has a pullLines paragraph, and that paragraph is not the block's last. Three owner actions break this. (1) Ticking «تظهر المقاطع هنا» on a movement with no large line. (2) Correcting a typo in the display paragraph of the 2020 movement without also editing the matching pullLines entry, which needs an exact match and is not validated; if no display line remains in block 0, the films are gone. (3) A movement whose first paragraph is a band line: block 0 is then a band, so both the films and the movement's vignette (withFigure) are dropped. In all three cases the family films vanish from /started while the admin still shows them as placed there.
findings.suggestedFix: In StartedRoomView.tsx Movement, key on the first text block (`const firstText = blocks.findIndex((x) => x.kind === 'text')`) instead of `b === 0`. When movement.films is set, render `<Films>` for that block even if splitAfterFirstDisplay returns an empty `after`: put it after `before` when there is no display split.
verifierCorrections: Use `const firstText = blocks.findIndex((x) => x.kind === 'text')` for both withFigure and the films split. When movement.films is set and `after` is empty, still render <Films> right after the first text block's Band (and put the closing after the films if that block is also the last). This avoids duplicating the render path.

findings.title: When the server rejects an email the form accepted (422), the visitor gets a generic error with no field marked
findings.evidence:

...

Server: EMAIL_SHAPE = /^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]{1,64}@[A-Za-z0-9.-]{1,190}\.(?:[A-Za-z]{2,63}|xn--...)$/ -> fail(422, 'INVALID', 'بيانات غير صالحة.', parsed.error.flatten())

findings.title: Media-id lookups put every id in one GET URL; at about 420 post covers the build fails with 414
findings.failureScenario: Each UUID adds about 39 URL characters once URLSearchParams encodes the comma as %2C. At about 420 visible posts with media-library covers, the request passes the 16 KB URL limit of Cloudflare, which fronts hosted Supabase (ISSUES I32). The GET answers 414, mediaById throws 'Failed to fetch media: 414', and from then on every publish fails the site build. VERIFICATION.md:55 names 500 posts as the representative load. content.ts resolveMedia and store.ts resolveCovers repeat the same single-request pattern.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the lookup into one helper in src/lib/content.ts that fetches ids in chunks of about 100 and merges the maps. Use it from journal.ts mediaById and store.ts resolveCovers instead of their two copies.
verifierCorrections: Fix together with X6.13. Export one `mediaById(ids)` from content.ts that splits the ids into chunks of about 100, runs the GETs, and merges the rows into one Map. Use it in resolveMedia, journal.ts and store.ts resolveCovers. Store's empty-derivatives filter can go, because replaceMediaIds already skips empty derivatives (content.ts:102).
